purpose: Provenance ledger for four distilled units covering Ascend HCCL transport and rank-table invariants, HCCL wait-timeout triage, PD-disaggregated KV transfer, and multi-node MoE expert parallelism with MC2 and All2All.

claims: A2, A3 and A5 keep intra-node and inter-node transports in separate domains; the inter-node domain is RoCE v2.
A3 exposes two dies per card and sixteen logic devices per eight-card node; npu-smi distinguishes Chip Logic ID from Chip Phy-ID.
rank_table_file v1.0 binds node-local device_id, cluster-global rank_id and per-device RoCE device_ip.
HCCL_BUFFSIZE is a per-communicator MB capacity contract, defaulting to 200 MB, and must be equal on all ranks.
HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME selects the host NIC used for HCCL socket bootstrap; it is not the NPU device IP.
HCCL_INTRA_ROCE_ENABLE=1 moves intra-node traffic to RDMA; it does not change the inter-node transport or create a SuperPod.

supporting_ranges.claim: A3 dual-die cards: 16 cards x 2 dies = 32 die-level ranks; die-level parallelism is explicit.
950PR/950DT are the A5 generation; deployment counts and platform branches differ from A3.
A2 is checked over device ids 0..7 and A3 over 0..15; link, optical, lldp, net_health and ping use hccn_tool.
Cross-machine LLM-DataDist rank table uses server_count=2, one device per server, device_id local and rank_id global 0/1.
Single-machine rank table keeps two devices under one server with device ids local and rank ids 0/1.
HCCL_BUFFSIZE default 200 MB; too-small error; all ranks must agree.
MC2 dispatch/combine buffer formula and operator-side tiling failure when the buffer is too small.
A2 server / A3 supernode default to HCCS; HCCL_INTRA_ROCE_ENABLE=1 forces RDMA; device memory registration is 2 MiB aligned.

limitations: A5 device enumeration is deliberately not asserted; it must be read from the installed npu-smi output.
The unit is a hardware/runtime contract, not a benchmark; no latency or bandwidth number is claimed.
A3 superpod fabric naming and A5 node fabric naming are installation-specific; only the separation from RoCE v2 is asserted.

claims: EI0006 is Get_Socket_Timeout; EI0002 is a notify-wait timeout whose default collective timeout is 1800 s; HCCL_E_WAIT_TIMEOUT is the same wait-timeout family.
A wait timeout is a secondary symptom until all-rank logs prove that every rank entered the collective.
One rank that crashes, exits, skips a collective on an idle DP batch, or has a different collective ledger produces a timeout on the peers without a physical link fault.
Physical degradation is separated with hccn_tool link, optical, stat, lldp and ping on the waiting peer's device.
Raising HCCL_EXEC_TIMEOUT before classifying participation versus link health masks the fault.

supporting_ranges.claim: EI0006 is often secondary; grep all rank logs for an earlier OOM or crash; ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING can localize.
Every rank must enter the same collective sequence; idle DP batches need a dummy forward; local-state-gated collectives diverge.
Documented hccn_tool checks: lldp for peer switch port, link for UP/DOWN, net_health, netdetect, gateway, ip and ping.
Optical module, RoCE link UP, local NPU IP and remote NPU ping are the four physical checks before a device-direct transfer.
HCCL environment checks are read-only and must report actual paths, exit codes and missing items rather than infer a pass.

limitations: The SOP is a source- and runbook-derived software contract; no live NPU triage was performed for this unit.
EI0002's default 1800 s is a timeout budget, not a diagnosis; workload skew can legitimately exceed it.
hccn_tool output fields vary by driver and platform; interpret the actual command output rather than assuming a schema.

claims: MooncakeConnector requires prefill_tp_size >= decode_tp_size and computes tp_num_need_pulls from the per-rank KV-head counts.
The transferred asymmetric-TP KV layout is [block, split, token, head_per_split, dim] and must be restored to [block, token, split, head_per_split, dim] before attention consumes it.
A pull-based P/D connector must delay P-side block release until every distinct decode TP rank has acknowledged; duplicate acknowledgements must not count.
A request rejected before scheduler admission must still send an empty completion so the P node can release stranded blocks.
Abort and timeout reclamation must be verified by free-block count and by fault injection, not by the presence of a delete API.

supporting_ranges.claim: request_finished delays free, enqueues an empty receive for pre-admission rejection, and exports remote_ptp_size.
MooncakeConnectorWorker rejects prefill_tp_size < decode_tp_size and computes tp_num_need_pulls from num_key_value_heads.
Asymmetric-TP KV is transposed from [block, split, token, head_per_split, dim] to [block, token, split, head_per_split, dim].
Delayed free requests are force-released after VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT.
Pull-based P/D release needs a distinct-decode-rank ACK barrier, duplicate-rank dedup, and synchronous handshake; CDCP push is an alternative.
Only store connector needs register_buffer=true to produce mem type:1 device registration; torchair KV is 3-D and needs an adaptive block rank.
Mooncake Ascend direct needs USE_ASCEND_DIRECT, set_device before engine construction, positional initialize, and 2 MiB alignment on the HCCS IPC path.
LLM-DataDist link uses a v1.0 rank table and polls query_register_mem_status until RegisterMemStatus.OK.

limitations: The 4P+4D A3 baseline is recorded in the private transcript digest; exact model, image, host names and throughput are intentionally not reproduced here.
The LlmDataDist pull path is source-reviewed through its public contract and examples; it was not independently rerun for this unit.
Free-block accounting proves logical reclamation, not physical HBM release; allocator-level release remains unverified.
Mooncake and LlmDataDist are different connectors with different configuration surfaces; do not mix their fixes.

claims: Multi-node MoE EP admission must prove divisibility (batch/EP, experts/EP, SP length/attn-TP) and the A2 experts-per-rank ceiling before selecting MC2.
Prefill and decode should use different All2All paths: double-routing for large prefill token counts and MC2 dispatch/combine for small-batch EP decode.
MC2 dispatch/combine needs a dedicated HCCL communicator, a sufficient HCCL_BUFFSIZE, and comm_alg=fullmesh_v2 only where zero experts are absent.
Convergence requires a non-EP golden, routing-weight preservation, inverse-mapping integrity, and equal collective participation across DP ranks.
Scale-up is gated on repeated soak and fault-injection results, not on a single successful request.

supporting_ranges.claim: MC2 dispatch/combine contract, A2 experts-per-rank ceiling, zero-expert support, dedicated communicator and fullmesh_v2 caveats.
MC2 cannot share a communicator; moe_ep_group_mc2 is dedicated and buffers are sized per domain.
Prefill uses double-routing All2All; decode uses MC2; A2 or eager falls back.
copy_expert_num handles zero experts inside MC2; fullmesh_v2 is incompatible with zero experts.
MC2 buffer formula and the operator tiling failure when HCCL_BUFFSIZE is too small.
batch must divide moe_ep_size; SP prefill length must align to attn_tp_size.
DP+EP ranks must align prefill/decode phase, run dummy work when idle, and replace variable-length collectives with fixed-length ones on multi-machine.
All2All-v split arrays come from non-blocking D2H; the single-expert branch needs an explicit device sync before the async collective reads them.

limitations: Multi-node A3/A5 EP runs are recorded in the private transcript digest; no throughput or accuracy number is claimed here.
A2's experts-per-rank ceiling and A3's absence are source-documented; A5 MC2 limits must be confirmed against the installed operator version.
The workflow is a convergence procedure, not a guarantee that fullmesh_v2 is beneficial for a given topology.
